evidence: Reactive insufficiency is argued from timing physics and corroborated in simulation. (1) Lead-time: burst onsets ramp baseline-to-peak in a median of 6 minutes; against replica cold starts of tens of seconds to minutes, a third of bursts arrive too fast for a policy that waits to observe them (trace-EDA). (2) Averaging cannot rescue it: the arrival process is overdispersed at every operational scale (Fano factor grows ~3 orders of magnitude with the counting window), so no averaging window makes a threshold rule safe. (3) Direct evidence: v_infraction shows reactive-policy language runs violating the ITL p99=100ms bound (e.g. a11:burst3_reactive_L60 -> 160 ms; reactive:r32A_burst1 -> 129 ms; reactive:r32B_burst2 -> 127 ms) while forecast runs on the same windows pass (~5 ms); and the closed-loop narrative states the reactive controller on the SAME (correct) signal loses the fastest-onset burst at every lead. So even with the right signal, reactive scaling is insufficient because it observes the onset too late. Mechanism (onset speed vs actuation latency) is warranted.
